claims.text: AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an older execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it ever starts (the lock only protects an execution once it is running).

In a CodePipeline pipeline using `SUPERSEDED` mode whose CodeBuild stage runs `pulumi up`, a queued execution waiting behind a busy stage can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting a CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
To use `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set when defining the pipeline, via the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline`/`update-pipeline` commands.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack concurrently, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
The page links to /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ as the page describing Pulumi update conflicts.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check that can be applied to the environment targeted by a deployment job, preventing concurrent runs from deploying to the same environment.
The Microsoft Learn page at learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals documents the Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
Azure Pipelines YAML supports a `lockBehavior` property set at the stage level that controls how the stage behaves with respect to exclusive lock checks on environments it references.
`lockBehavior` accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
The `Pulumi@1` Azure Pipelines task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` (e.g. `args: --yes`).
`runLatest` is the default value of `lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines.

With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting behind it are passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually being applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run is run against the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
The page links to /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ as the docs for the `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource.

When two runs of the same TeamCity build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let a build configuration run concurrently against as many free agents as are available, so nothing prevents concurrent runs of the same build configuration by default.
The Pulumi documentation page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes update conflicts.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds', located under the configuration's General Settings.
The TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0, which means unlimited.

Setting the TeamCity option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud's per-stack update lease gives the same one-at-a-time behavior as limiting TeamCity concurrent builds to 1, i.e. only one update at a time can run against a stack.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments so they don't run concurrently.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage makes runs waiting on an exclusive lock proceed sequentially (queued in turn) rather than only the latest run proceeding.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ exists and has a section anchored at #serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ exists and has a section anchored at #serialize-pipeline-executions.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes deployment builds.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ exists and has a section anchored at #limit-concurrent-builds.
